newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends up at year high on GM jv.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends up at year high on GM jv.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index continued its bull run to end up at a 1997 high on Wednesday on news that General Motors Corp and a Shanghai company had signed a $1.57 billion production deal, brokers said.
The B share index rose 1.318 points or 1.84 percent to 72.941 points on volume of 21.4 million shares worth $10.7 million against $9.4 million on Tuesday.
GM and state-owned Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp singed on Tuesday a $1.57 billion joint venture to produce cars in the Jinqiao Export Processing Zone, in Shanghai's Pudong New Area.
Real estate developer Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development was the third biggest winner on the news, rising $0.026 or 4.81 percent to $0.566 on volume of 952,800 shares.
Brokers said that a strong performance by Pudong shares gave the market further confidence, and most investors wanted to build positions in stocks with solid results records.
"Market sentiment has improved and buying has focused on stocks with good records as most firms 1996 results have yet to be released and the market is in the dark," one broker said.
"Technical charts indicate the index will move towards the 75-point resistance level in the coming days," one broker said.
All 43 B shares traded, with 26 up, 11 flat and six down.
Shanghai Dazhong Taxi was the star on expectations of good 1996 results and talk of an attractive bonus offer plan, soaring $0.102 or 10 percent to its limit up of $1.122 on volume of 444,000 shares.
Toy maker Shanghai Haixin traded the most on talk of its good 1996 results, gaining $0.036 or 6.14 percent to $0.622 on volume of 2.2 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index continued its rises on bullish market sentiment with active buying in selective stocks, brokers said.

The A index rose 18.172 points or 1.45 percent to 1,272.889 points on volume of 839.6 million shares worth 9.5 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue chip index gained 11.001 points or 0.32 percent to 3,493.479 points.

Tristar Petrochemical was the star on talk of a solid bonus offering plan, surging 1.89 yuan or 10 percent to its daily limit-up of 20.77 yuan on volume of 1.8 million shares. -- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
